mainTopic: What is included when one sells a city (the meaning of סנטר, villages, enclosures) and what is included when one sells a field
overview: The משנה says that someone who sells a city sells its שלחין, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds the סנטר. The גמרא first shows how the view that סנטר means the land registrar fits the משנה: שלחין means the fields, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that the registrar is sold too. It then tries to prove from a ברייתא of רבי יהודה that סנטר is a person. It rejects that proof, finds a clash with the end of the same ברייתא, and reverses רבי יהודה's words. That reversal makes רבי יהודה agree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about the fields while he still disagrees about the nearby villages. Next, two ברייתות contradict each other about animal enclosures. The גמרא explains that enclosures facing the city are sold with it and those facing away are not, and it rereads the line about the woods to fit this. The amud ends with a new משנה about which items are sold together with a field.

steps.title: How does the registrar view fit the משנה's dispute?
steps.stepSummary: If סנטר means the land registrar, why would רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answer the תנא קמא's 'gardens' with 'the registrar'? The two don't seem connected.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says סנטר is the land registrar: the תנא קמא said 'gardens,' and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answers him 'the registrar'?! How do these connect?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a problem on the view that סנטר means the land registrar. A dispute should be about the same subject, but gardens and a registrar have nothing to do with each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a משנה, when רבן שמעון בן גמליאל speaks after the תנא קמא, he is usually responding to what the תנא קמא said. If the תנא קמא was talking about gardens (שלחין) and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל talks about a person, there is no real dispute between them. So the 'registrar' reading looks hard to fit into the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The land registrar, the official who knows and points out the borders of fields
The word in the משנה whose meaning is being argued about
Gardens
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
And he responds to him

phrases.english: But according to the one who says it means the land registrar –
phrases.notes: The 'it' is the word סנטר from the משנה.

phrases.english: the first תנא said: gardens;

phrases.aramaic: וּמַהְדַּר לֵיהּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל:
phrases.english: and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel responds to him:
the land registrar?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing earlier on the daf how the 'fields' view fits the משנה, the גמרא now tests the 'registrar' view the same way.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that סנטר means the land registrar
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's two opinions should be about the same subject, but gardens and a registrar are unrelated.

steps.title: שלחין means fields, so the registrar is something extra
steps.stepSummary: שלחין does not mean gardens but the fields around the city. The תנא קמא says the fields are sold but not the registrar, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that even the registrar is sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think שלחין means gardens? No, שלחין means fields, as it says 'and sends water upon the fields.' The fields are sold, but the registrar is not. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל comes to say that even the registrar is sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing how we read the word שלחין in the משנה. Once שלחין means fields, the registrar fits as a natural next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא קמא is talking about the fields, then a dispute about the registrar makes sense, because the registrar is the man who keeps track of those fields. The תנא קמא sells only the fields, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the registrar comes along with them. A פסוק backs up the reading of שלחין as fields.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in the משנה, here understood as the fields around the city
Fields, farmland
Is sold (along with the city)
Do you think...? (opening to correct an assumption)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the 'registrar' view, שלחין means fields, and the dispute is whether the registrar goes along with the sale of the city.

phrases.english: Do you think that what שלחין means is gardens?!
No; what does שלחין mean? Fields,
as it is written: 'and sends water upon the fields';
phrases.notes: איוב 5:10. The word וְשֹׁלֵחַ sounds like שלחין, linking it to fields.

phrases.english: but the land registrar is not sold.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְמֵימַר,
phrases.english: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel comes to say
that even the land registrar is also sold.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the משנה (שלחין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלחין means gardens, so a dispute about the registrar seems unconnected.
steps.terutzMaskana: שלחין means fields; the תנא קמא sells only the fields, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds the registrar.

steps.title: A proof from רבי יהודה that סנטר is a person
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says in the name of רבי יהודה that the סנטר is not sold but the אנקולמוס (city scribe) is sold. Since the scribe is a person, the סנטר listed next to him should also be a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says, the סנטר is not sold, the city scribe is sold. Isn't it clear that since the scribe is a man, the סנטר is also a man?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to prove that סנטר means a person (the registrar), not fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that things listed together are usually the same kind of thing. The אנקולמוס is clearly a person, so the סנטר mentioned right beside him should also be a person. That would support the 'registrar' view against the 'fields' view.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introducing a source as proof)
The city scribe
A man, a person
Sold

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The santar is not sold, the city scribe is sold.
What, is it not that since the city scribe is a man,
the santar is also a man?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having shown both views fit the משנה, the גמרא looks for an outside source to decide between them.
steps.raayaObject: That סנטר means a person (the land registrar)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה listing סנטר next to אנקולמוס

steps.title: Being listed together does not prove they are the same kind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: each item stands on its own. The scribe can be a person while the סנטר means fields.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a proof?! This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 3. Just because two things are mentioned side by side does not mean they are the same type of thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the idea that items in one list must be alike. The גמרא says no: the אנקולמוס is a person, and the סנטר can still mean fields. So the 'fields' view survives, and the ברייתא now reads as: the fields are not sold, the scribe is sold.

keyTerms.meaning: Are these comparable? (a way to reject a proof)
This one is as it is and that one is as it is; each case stands on its own

phrases.english: Are they comparable?!
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
phrases.notes: He means: the scribe is a person, and the סנטר can still be the fields.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not the 'registrar' view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Items listed side by side don't have to be the same kind of thing.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא implies the fields are sold
steps.stepSummary: If סנטר means fields and רבי יהודה says it is not sold, that clashes with the end of the same ברייתא, which says only the leftover strips of field are not sold, implying the main fields are sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you say that? The end of the ברייתא teaches: but not its remnants, not its daughter villages, not the woods set aside for it, and not the enclosures for animals, birds, and fish. And we explained: what are 'its remnants'? בִּיזְלֵי. What are בִּיזְלֵי? רבי אבא said: strips of fields. So only strips of fields are not sold, but the fields themselves are sold!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 4 (סנטר = fields, not sold) by looking at the later part of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the ברייתא lists what is not sold with the city, including 'its remnants,' which רבי אבא explains as small cut-off strips of field. If only the strips are left out, then the main fields must be included in the sale. That contradicts reading רבי יהודה as saying the fields (סנטר) are not sold.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really say this? (opening a challenge)
The later part of a source
Its remnants (leftover pieces)
Separated strips or bits of land
Strips of fields cut off from the main fields
Enclosures for keeping animals, birds, or fish

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not on the proof itself but on the reading left after step 4: that רבי יהודה says the fields are not sold.

phrases.english: And can you say this?
phrases.notes: 'This' means: that רבי יהודה holds the fields are not sold.

phrases.english: But it teaches in the later part:
but not its remnants and not its daughters,
phrases.notes: 'Daughters' are the small villages near the city.

phrases.english: and not the woods set aside for it,
and not the enclosures for animals
and for birds and for fish.
And we said: what are 'its remnants'? Bizlei.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי בִּיזְלֵי? אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: פִּיסְקֵי בָּגֵי.
phrases.english: What are bizlei? Rabbi Abba said: strips of fields.
It is strips of fields that are not sold,
but the fields themselves are sold!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the ברייתא that step 4 left standing.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רבי יהודה as 'the fields (סנטר) are not sold'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The later part of the same ברייתא excludes only strips of fields, implying the main fields are sold, which contradicts the earlier part.

steps.title: Reverse רבי יהודה's statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the contradiction by switching the words: רבי יהודה says the סנטר (fields) is sold, and the scribe is not sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it: רבי יהודה says, the סנטר is sold, the city scribe is not sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by flipping the wording of רבי יהודה's statement in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once reversed, the ברייתא is consistent: the fields (סנטר) are sold with the city, and the later part only leaves out the small cut-off strips. The scribe, a person, is not included in the sale. This keeps the 'fields' meaning of סנטר.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it (switch the wording of a source)

steps.whatToRemember: With the reversal, רבי יהודה holds the fields (סנטר) are sold with the city but the scribe is not, which fits the later part of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Reverse it –
Rabbi Yehuda says: the santar is sold,
the city scribe is not sold.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the wording of a source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה says the סנטר is not sold, which clashes with the later part of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה says the סנטר (fields) is sold and the scribe is not, so the ברייתא is consistent.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really agree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the switched version. In the same ברייתא, רבי יהודה says the villages around the city are not sold, which is the view of the רבנן against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say רבי יהודה holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל? He holds like the רבנן! The end of his ברייתא says the leftover strips and the nearby villages are not sold. But רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that whoever sells a city also sells its villages, as another ברייתא teaches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the fix from the last step. That fix made רבי יהודה sound like he agrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, but elsewhere in the same ברייתא he clearly disagrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the switch, רבי יהודה says the fields (סנטר) are sold, just like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. But the end of the same ברייתא has רבי יהודה saying the בנות (nearby villages) are not sold. Another ברייתא shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds the בנות are sold, so רבי יהודה seems to side with the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Its leftovers: the leftover strips of field around the city
Its 'daughters': the small villages that depend on the city
The end part of a ברייתא or משנה
The Sages: the majority opinion that argues with a named rabbi

phrases.english: And can you really say

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה – כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סְבִירָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yehuda holds like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה כְּרַבָּנַן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: But Rabbi Yehuda holds like the Rabbis!
As the end of that ברייתא teaches:
But not its leftover strips and not its 'daughters.'
phrases.notes: 'Daughters' here means the small villages around the city.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, הָאָמַר:
phrases.english: Whereas Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, doesn't he say:
If he sold the city, he sold its daughters!

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הָעִיר – לָא מָכַר אֶת בְּנוֹתֶיהָ.
phrases.english: As a ברייתא teaches: one who sells the city has not sold its daughters.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One who sells the city has sold its daughters!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the switched wording from step 6, which makes רבי יהודה agree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fix from step 6, where רבי יהודה says the סנטר (fields) is sold.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה rules that the בנות are not sold, which goes against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. So it seems unlikely that he agrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about the fields.

steps.title: רבי יהודה agrees on one point and disagrees on another
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה can agree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that the fields are sold, and still disagree with him about the villages.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה agrees with him on one point and disagrees with him on one point.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A rabbi does not have to agree with someone on everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the fields around the city (סנטר), רבי יהודה agrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that they are sold. On the villages (בנות), he sides with the רבנן that they are not sold. So the switched wording from step 6 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like him; he agrees with him
On one point
He disagrees with him

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה (after the switch): the fields around the city ARE sold, like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. The villages are NOT sold, like the רבנן.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּווֹתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda agrees with him on one point,
phrases.notes: The one point is the fields around the city: both say they are sold.

phrases.english: and disagrees with him on one point.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לֵיהּ כְּווֹתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא, וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by splitting רבי יהודה's view into two separate issues.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the issues: agreement on one, disagreement on the other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבי יהודה disagrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל about the villages, he must disagree about the fields too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each issue is separate. רבי יהודה agrees about the fields and disagrees about the villages.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about animal enclosures
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says the enclosures for animals, birds, and fish are not sold with a city. Another ברייתא says they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said the enclosures for animals, birds, and fish are not sold. But another ברייתא teaches: if the city has villages, they are not sold with it. If it has one part in the sea and one part on dry land, or enclosures for animals, birds, and fish, these are sold with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the earlier ברייתא about the animal enclosures and shows another ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא lists the ביברין (enclosures) as things that are NOT included when a city is sold. The second ברייתא lists the very same enclosures as things that ARE included. Both cannot be true as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Enclosures or pens for keeping animals, birds, or fish
And contrast it with: introduces a source that contradicts
Dry land

phrases.english: 'And not the enclosures for animals,'
'and for birds and for fish.'
And contrast it with this:

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ לָהּ בָּנוֹת – אֵין נִמְכָּרוֹת עִמָּהּ.
phrases.english: If the city had daughter villages, they are not sold with it.
If it had one part in the sea
and one part on dry land;

phrases.aramaic: בֵּיבָרִים שֶׁל חַיָּה וְשֶׁל עוֹפוֹת וְשֶׁל דָּגִים –
phrases.english: enclosures for animals, for birds, and for fish:
these are sold with it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the רבי יהודה discussion to a new item in the same ברייתא: the enclosures.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the enclosures are not sold with the city.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא says the same enclosures are sold with the city, a direct contradiction.

steps.title: It depends on which way the enclosure faces
steps.stepSummary: The two ברייתות are talking about different enclosures. One kind faces in toward the city and the other faces out.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. This one faces inward, and that one faces outward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by saying each ברייתא is talking about a different kind of enclosure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An enclosure that faces inward, toward the city, counts as part of the city and is sold with it. An enclosure that faces outward, away from the city, is not part of it and is not sold. So both ברייתות are right, each about its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a problem: the two sources speak about different cases
Facing or turned toward
Inward
Outward

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
this one is where it faces inward,
phrases.notes: Facing in toward the city: this is the ברייתא that says the enclosures are sold.

phrases.english: and that one is where it faces outward.
phrases.notes: Facing away from the city: this is the ברייתא that says they are not sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; הָא דִּנְגִיחַ קַאיְהִי לְגָו, וְהָא דִּנְגִיחַ קַאיְהִי לְבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 9 by splitting the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two sources talk about different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות give opposite rules about the same enclosures.
steps.terutzMaskana: Inward-facing enclosures are sold with the city. Outward-facing ones are not.

steps.title: The woods 'set aside for' the city are not sold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the ברייתא says woods that are 'set aside for' the city are not sold. That sounds like they belong to the city, yet they are not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches: 'And not the woods that are set aside for it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that being connected to the city makes something part of the sale. It points to the woods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Based on step 10, anything that faces or belongs to the city should be sold with it. Yet the ברייתא says woods 'set aside for' the city are not sold. This seems to break the rule just given.

keyTerms.meaning: Woods or groves of trees
That are set aside for it (for the city)

phrases.english: But it teaches:
'And not the woods that are set aside for it'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָא תָנֵי: וְלֹא אֶת חוֹרָשִׁין הַמּוּקְצִין לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from step 10 using another item in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that things facing or connected to the city are sold with it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The woods are described as 'set aside for' the city, so they seem connected to it, yet the ברייתא says they are not sold.

steps.title: Read it as woods set apart from the city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording: the woods are 'set apart from' the city, meaning far away. That is why they are not sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'that are set apart from it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by adjusting one word in the ברייתא. The woods are distant from the city, not connected to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By reading 'from it' instead of 'for it,' the woods become separate from the city. Since they are not connected, they are not sold. That fits the rule of step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: Say: read the text this way instead
That are set apart from it (far from the city)

steps.whatToRemember: What is connected to and facing the city is sold with it. What faces away from it or is set apart from it is not sold.
steps.confusionAlert: Only one word changes here: 'for it' (לָהּ) becomes 'from it' (הֵימֶנָּה). That small change flips the woods from 'belonging to the city' to 'separate from the city.'

phrases.english: Say: 'that are set apart from it.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is adjusting the wording: read it as woods that are distant from the city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by changing the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The woods are 'set aside for' the city and connected to it, yet they are not sold.
steps.terutzMaskana: The woods are 'set apart from' the city, so they are not connected and are not sold.

steps.title: Items automatically sold with a field
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the things that count as part of a field and go to the buyer even if they were never mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who sells a field also sells the stones and reeds that serve it, the grain still growing in the ground, a small patch of reeds, a simple watch hut, an ungrafted carob tree, and a young sycamore.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It lists what a buyer gets along with a field even if the sale did not spell it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that ties the list together is that these things serve the field or are attached to it, so they are treated as part of it. Every item comes with a condition ('for its use,' 'attached,' 'less than a בית רובע,' 'not plastered,' 'not grafted'). Those conditions set up the contrast in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: For its use, meaning it serves the field
Attached to the ground, still growing
A cluster or patch of reeds
An area big enough to sow a quarter of a קב of seed
A watchman's hut in the field
A young sycamore that has never been cut back

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets the basic rule for sales of land: things that serve the land or are attached to it go with it unless something else is said.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who sells the field,
has sold the stones that are for its use,
and the reeds in the vineyard that are for its use,
and the grain that is attached to the ground,
and the cluster of reeds
that is less than a beit rova,
phrases.notes: A בית רובע is the area you could sow with a quarter of a קב of seed. Below that size, the reed patch is just part of the field.

phrases.english: and the watch hut that is not made with clay,
and the carob tree that is not grafted,
and the young sycamore.
phrases.notes: Literally 'the virgin of the sycamore.' It means a young tree that has never been cut back.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוֹכֵר אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה מָכַר אֶת הָאֲבָנִים שֶׁהֵם לְצׇרְכָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה about selling a field, after the previous discussion about selling a city.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plain sale of a field includes things that serve it or are attached to it: useful stones and reeds, growing grain, a reed patch smaller than a בית רובע, an unplastered watch hut, an ungrafted carob, and a young sycamore.

steps.title: Items not sold with the field in a plain sale
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the opposite cases: stones and reeds that do not serve the field, and grain already cut, stay with the seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: He has not sold stones or vineyard reeds that are not used for the field, and he has not sold grain that has already been harvested.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the other side of the first three items. These things are in the field, but they are not part of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item mirrors one from the first list, with one change. The stones and reeds no longer serve the field, and the grain is no longer attached to the ground. Without that link to the field, they are only objects lying on it, so a plain sale does not include them.

keyTerms.meaning: That are not for its use
Detached, already harvested

phrases.english: But he has not sold
the stones that are not for its use,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַקָּנִים שֶׁבַּכֶּרֶם שֶׁאֵינָן לְצׇרְכּוֹ,
phrases.english: nor the reeds in the vineyard that are not for its use,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַתְּבוּאָה שֶׁהִיא תְּלוּשָׁה מִן הַקַּרְקַע.
phrases.english: nor the grain that is detached from the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל לֹא מָכַר לֹא אֶת הָאֲבָנִים שֶׁאֵינָן לְצׇרְכָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite cases for the first three items of step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a plain sale, stones and reeds that don't serve the field, and grain that has been cut, are not sold.

steps.title: Saying 'the field and everything in it' includes the extras
steps.stepSummary: If the seller says he is selling the field and everything in it, the items from step 14 are sold as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he told the buyer, 'I am selling it and everything inside it,' then all of these items are sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a twist. With the right wording, the seller can include the items that a plain sale leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the question was what counts as part of the field. Now the seller's words make the sale wider. 'Everything in it' covers loose stones, unused reeds, and cut grain, even though they are not part of the field itself.

keyTerms.meaning: It and everything that is in it
Sold

steps.confusionAlert: 'כּוּלָּן' here means the items from step 14, the ones a plain sale leaves out. It does not include the big items in the next step.

phrases.english: When he said to him:
"It and everything that is in it,"
then all of them are sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּזְמַן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הִיא וְכׇל מַה שֶּׁבְּתוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the seller's wording can include the items step 14 left out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'it and everything in it' includes even the items that do not serve the field and the grain that was already cut.

steps.title: Items never sold with the field, whatever was said
steps.stepSummary: A large reed patch, a plastered watch hut, a grafted carob, and a sycamore trunk are not sold with the field, even if the seller said 'everything in it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, with or without 'everything in it,' he has not sold a reed patch of a בית רובע, a watch hut plastered with clay, a grafted carob tree, or a sycamore trunk.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a group of items that never go with the field, whatever words the seller uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the larger versions of the last items in step 13. A reed patch of a בית רובע counts as its own field. A plastered hut is a real building. A grafted carob and a cut-back sycamore trunk are valuable on their own. Because they stand on their own, 'everything in it' does not reach them.

keyTerms.meaning: Either way, in both cases
Grafted
A sycamore trunk that has been cut back and grows new branches
Clay or plaster

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has three levels. Things that serve the field or are attached to it are always sold. Loose things in the field are sold only if the seller says 'everything in it.' Things that are significant on their own are never sold with the field.

phrases.english: Either way,
phrases.notes: Either a plain sale or a sale where he said 'everything in it.'

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מָכַר לֹא אֶת חִיצַת הַקָּנִים שֶׁהִיא בֵּית רוֹבַע,
phrases.english: he has not sold the cluster of reeds that is a beit rova,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא אֶת הַשּׁוֹמֵירָה שֶׁהִיא עֲשׂוּיָה בְּטִיט,
phrases.english: nor the watch hut that is made with clay,
nor the grafted carob tree,
nor the sycamore trunk.
phrases.notes: This is the opposite of the young sycamore in step 13. It is a tree that has been cut back to the trunk so it grows new branches.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ לֹא מָכַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on step 15: even 'everything in it' does not include these items, which are the larger versions of the last items in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A reed patch of a בית רובע, a plastered watch hut, a grafted carob, and a sycamore trunk are never sold with the field, even if the seller says 'everything in it.'
